entries.fc721b79cad2c87f67e86cd7052d9a8bcd057810: <reference osisRef="Neh.9.9-Neh.9.11">Neh 9:9-11</reference> “And Thou sawest the affliction of our fathers in Egypt, and heardest their cry by the Red Sea: <reference osisRef="Neh.9.10">Neh 9:10</reference> And showedst signs and wonders upon Pharaoh and all his servants, and on all the people of his land, because Thou knewest that they dealt proudly against them, and madest Thyself a name, as this day. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.11">Neh 9:11</reference> And Thou dividedst the sea before them, and they went through the midst of the sea on dry land; and their persecutors Thou threwest into the deeps, as a stone into the mighty waters.” In <reference osisRef="Neh.9.9">Neh 9:9</reference> are comprised two subjects, which are carried out in <reference osisRef="Neh.9.10">Neh 9:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Neh.9.11">Neh 9:11</reference> : (<reference osisRef="Neh.9.1">1</reference>) the affliction of the Israelites in Egypt, which God saw (comp. <reference osisRef="Exod.3.7">Exo 3:7</reference>), and out of which He delivered them by the signs and wonders He showed upon Pharaoh (<reference osisRef="Neh.9.10">Neh 9:10</reference>); (<reference osisRef="Neh.9.2">2</reference>) the crying for help at the Red Sea, when the Israelites perceived Pharaoh with his horsemen and chariots in pursuit (<reference osisRef="Exod.14.10">Exo 14:10</reference>), and the help which God gave them by dividing the sea, etc. (<reference osisRef="Neh.9.11">Neh 9:11</reference>). The words in <hi type="italic"><reference osisRef="Neh.9.10">Neh 9:10</reference></hi> are supported by <reference osisRef="Deut.6.22">Deu 6:22</reference>, on the ground of the historical narrative, Ex 7-10. The expression עליהם הזידוּ כּי is formed according to עליהם זדוּ אשׁר, Exo 18:11. על הזיד occurs <reference osisRef="Exod.21.14">Exo 21:14</reference> in a general sense. On וגו שׁם לך ותּעשׂ comp. <reference osisRef="Jer.32.20">Jer 32:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.58.12">Isa 58:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.58.14">Isa 58:14</reference>; 1Ch 17:22. A name as this day - in that the miracles which God then did are still praised, and He continues still to manifest His almighty power. The words of <reference osisRef="Neh.9.11">Neh 9:11</reference> are supported by <reference osisRef="Exod.14.21-Exod.14.22">Exo 14:21-22</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.14.28">Exo 14:28</reference>, and Exo 15:19. אבן כּמו בּמצולות are from <reference osisRef="Exod.15.5">Exo 15:5</reference>; עזּים בּמים from Ex 15 and Isa 43:16.
entries.5e8e72b7bb9fdf715862021313a9968eadf3ade0: <reference osisRef="Neh.9.12-Neh.9.15">Neh 9:12-15</reference> “And Thou leddest them in the day by a cloudy pillar, and in the night by a pillar of fire, to give them light in the way wherein they should go. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.13">Neh 9:13</reference> And Thou camest down upon mount Sinai, and spakest with them from heaven, and gavest them right judgments and true laws, good statutes and commandments: <reference osisRef="Neh.9.14">Neh 9:14</reference> And madest known unto them Thy holy Sabbath, and commandedst them precepts, statutes, and laws, by the hand of Moses Thy servant. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.15">Neh 9:15</reference> And gavest them bread from heaven for their hunger, and broughtest forth water for them out of the rock for their thirst; and Thou commandedst them to go in and possess the land, which Thou hadst lifted up Thine hand to give them.” Three particulars in the miraculous leading of Israel through the wilderness are brought forward: <hi type="italic">a</hi>. Their being guided in the way by miraculous tokens of the divine presence, in the pillar of fire and cloud, <reference osisRef="Neh.9.12">Neh 9:12</reference>; comp. <reference osisRef="Exod.13.21">Exo 13:21</reference>; Num 14:14. <hi type="italic">b</hi>. The revelation of God on Sinai, and the giving of the law, <reference osisRef="Neh.9.13">Neh 9:13</reference>, Neh 9:14. The descent of God on Sinai and the voice from heaven agree with <reference osisRef="Exod.19.18">Exo 19:18</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.19.20">Exo 19:20</reference>, and Exo 20:1., compared with Deu 4:36. On the various designations of the law, comp. <reference osisRef="Ps.19.9">Psa 19:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.119.43">Psa 119:43</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.119.39">Psa 119:39</reference>, Psa 119:142. Of the commandments, that concerning the Sabbath is specially mentioned, and spoken of as a benefit bestowed by God upon the Israelites, as a proclamation of His holy Sabbath, inasmuch as the Israelites were on the Sabbath to share in the rest of God; see rem. on <reference osisRef="Exod.20.9">Exo 20:9</reference>-11. <hi type="italic">c</hi>. The provision of manna, and of water from the rock, for their support during their journey through the wilderness on the way to Canaan; <reference osisRef="Exod.16.4">Exo 16:4</reference>, Exo 16:10., <reference osisRef="Exod.17.6">Exo 17:6</reference>; Num 20:8; comp. <reference osisRef="Ps.78.24">Psa 78:24</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.78.15">Psa 78:15</reference>; Psa 105:40. לרשׁת לבוא like <reference osisRef="Deut.9.1">Deu 9:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Deut.9.5">Deu 9:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.11.31">Deu 11:31</reference>, and elsewhere. את־ידך נשׂאת is to be understood according to Num 14:30. <div eID="gen6607" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen6608" type="x-p"/> Even the fathers to whom God had shown such favour, repeatedly departed from and rebelled against Him; but God of His great mercy did not forsake them, but brought them into possession of the promised land.
entries.b65be159ea55f75d89fd8e841945dc38b761ac2b: <reference osisRef="Neh.9.16-Neh.9.17">Neh 9:16-17</reference> “And they, even our fathers, dealt proudly, and hardened their necks, and hearkened not to Thy commandments. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.17">Neh 9:17</reference> They refused to obey, and were not mindful of Thy wonders that Thou didst amongst them; and hardened their necks, and appointed a captain to return to their bondage. But Thou art a God ready to pardon, gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and forsookest them not.” In these verses the conduct of the children of Israel towards God is contrasted with His kindness towards this stiff-necked people, the historical confirmation following in Neh 9:18. והם is emphatic, and prefixed to contrast the conduct of the Israelites with the benefits bestowed on them. The contrast is enhanced by the ו explicative before אבתינוּ, <hi type="italic">even</hi> our fathers (which J. D. Michaelis would expunge, from a misconception of its meaning, but which Bertheau with good reason defends). Words are accumulated to describe the stiff-necked resistance of the people. הזידוּ as above, Neh 9:10. “They hardened their necks” refers to <reference osisRef="Exod.32.9">Exo 32:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Exod.33.3">Exo 33:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Exod.34.9">Exo 34:9</reference>, and therefore already alludes to the worship of the golden calf at Sinai, mentioned <reference osisRef="Neh.9.18">Neh 9:18</reference>; while in <reference osisRef="Neh.9.17">Neh 9:17</reference>, the second great rebellion of the people at Kadesh, on the borders of the promised land, Num 14, is contemplated. The repetition of the expression, “they hardened their hearts,” shows that a second grievous transgression is already spoken of in Neh 9:17. This is made even clearer by the next clause, וגו ראשׁ ויּתּנוּ, which is taken almost verbally from Num 14:4 : “They said one to another, Let us make a captain (ראשׁ נתּנה), and return to Egypt;” the notion being merely enhanced here by the addition לעבדתם, to their bondage. The comparison with Num 14:4 also shows that בּמרים is a clerical error for בּמצרים, as the lxx read; for בּמרים, in their stubbornness, after לעבדתם, gives no appropriate sense. In spite, however, of their stiff-neckedness, God of His mercy and goodness did not forsake them. סליחות אלוהּ, a God of pardons; comp. <reference osisRef="Dan.9.9">Dan 9:9</reference>; Psa 130:4. וגו ורחוּם חנּוּן is a reminiscence of Exo 34:6. The ו before חסד came into the text by a clerical error.
entries.58876e792c0cf4b6c0c32385995ed5fe9c5e7847: <reference osisRef="Neh.9.18-Neh.9.21">Neh 9:18-21</reference> “Yea, they even made them a molten calf, and said, This is thy god that brought thee up out of Egypt, and wrought great provocations. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.19">Neh 9:19</reference> Yet Thou, in Thy manifold mercies, didst not forsake them in the wilderness; the pillar of the cloud departed not from them by day to lead them, and the pillar of fire by night to show them light in the way wherein they should go. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.20">Neh 9:20</reference> Thou gavest also Thy good Spirit to instruct them, and withheldest not Thy manna from their mouth, and gavest them water for their thirst: <reference osisRef="Neh.9.21">Neh 9:21</reference> And forty years didst Thou sustain them in the wilderness; they lacked nothing, their clothes waxed not old, and their feet swelled not.” כּי אף, also (even this) = yea even. On the worship of the golden calf, see Exo 24:4. The words ”they did (wrought) great provocations” involve a condemnation of the worship of the molten calf; nevertheless God did not withdraw His gracious presence, but continued to lead them by the pillar of cloud and fire. The passage Num 14:14, according to which the pillar of cloud and fire guided the march of the people through the wilderness after the departure from Sinai, i.e., after their transgression in the matter of the calf, is here alluded to. הענן עמּוּד is rhetorically enhanced by את: and with respect to the cloudy pillar, it departed not; so, too, in the second clause, האשׁ את־עמּוּד; comp. Ewald, §277, <hi type="italic">d</hi>. The words, <reference osisRef="Neh.9.20">Neh 9:20</reference>, “Thou gavest Thy good Spirit,” etc., refer to the occurrence, Num 11:17, Num 11:25, where God endowed the seventy elders with the spirit of prophecy for the confirmation of Moses’ authority. The definition “good Spirit” recalls Psa 143:10. The sending of manna is first mentioned Num 11:6-9, comp. <reference osisRef="Josh.5.12">Jos 5:12</reference>; the giving of water, Num 20:2-8. - In <reference osisRef="Neh.9.21">Neh 9:21</reference>, all that the Lord did for Israel is summed up in the assertion of <reference osisRef="Deut.2.7">Deu 2:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.8.4">Deu 8:4</reference>, חסרוּ לא; see the explanation of these passages.
entries.70b25d27360dd700cbc20550733133732111f25a: <reference osisRef="Neh.9.22-Neh.9.25">Neh 9:22-25</reference> <div eID="gen6608" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen6609" type="x-p"/> The Lord also fulfilled His promise of giving the land of Canaan to the Israelites notwithstanding their rebelliousness. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.22">Neh 9:22</reference> “And Thou gavest them kingdoms and nations, and didst divide them by boundaries; and they took possession of the land of Sihon, both the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.23">Neh 9:23</reference> And Thou didst multiply their children as the stars of heaven, and bring them into the land which Thou hadst promised to their fathers, that they should go in to possess. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.24">Neh 9:24</reference> And the children went in and possessed the land, and Thou subduedst before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and gavest them into their hands, both their kings and the people of the land, to do with them according to their pleasure. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.25">Neh 9:25</reference> And they took fortified cities, and a fat land, and took possession of houses filled with all kinds of goods, wells digged, vineyards and olive gardens, and fruit trees in abundance; and they ate and became fat, and delighted themselves in Thy great goodness.” לפאה ותּחלקם is variously explained. Aben Ezra and others refer the suffix to the Canaanites, whom God scattered <hi type="italic">in multos angulos or varias mundi partes</hi>. Others refer it to the Israelites. According to this view, Ramb. says: <hi type="italic">fecisti eos per omnes terrae Cananaeae angulos habitare;</hi> and Gusset.: <hi type="italic">distribuisti eis terram usque ad angulum h. l. nulla vel minima regionum particula excepta</hi>. But חלק, Piel, generally means the dividing of things; and when used of persons, as in <reference osisRef="Gen.49.7">Gen 49:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lam.4.16">Lam 4:16</reference>, to divide, to scatter, <hi type="italic">sensu malo</hi>, which is here inapplicable to the Israelites. חלק signifies to divide, especially by lot, and is used chiefly concerning the partition of the land of Canaan, in Kal, <reference osisRef="Josh.14.5">Jos 14:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Josh.18.2">Jos 18:2</reference>, and in Piel, <reference osisRef="Josh.13.7">Jos 13:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Josh.18.10">Jos 18:10</reference>; Jos 19:51. The word פּאה also frequently occurs in Joshua, in the sense of a corner or side lying towards a certain quarter of the heavens, and of a boundary; comp. <reference osisRef="Josh.15.5">Jos 15:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Josh.18.12">Jos 18:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Josh.18.14-Josh.18.15">Jos 18:14-15</reference>, Jos 18:20. According to this, Bertheau rightly takes the words to say: Thou didst divide them (the kingdoms and nations, i.e., the land of these nations) according to sides or boundaries, i.e., according to certain definite limits. Sihon is the king of Heshbon (<reference osisRef="Deut.1.4">Deu 1:4</reference>), and the ו before ח את־ארץ מ is not to be expunged as a gloss, but regarded as explicative: and, indeed, both the land of the king of Heshbon and the land of Og. The conquest of these two kingdoms is named first, because it preceded the possession of Canaan (Num 21:21-35). The increase of the children of the Israelites is next mentioned, <reference osisRef="Neh.9.23">Neh 9:23</reference>; the fathers having fallen in the wilderness, and only their children coming into the land of Canaan. The numbering of the people in the plains of Moab (Num 26) is here alluded to, when the new generation was found to be twice as numerous as that which marched out of Egypt; while the words לרשׁת לבוא, here and in <reference osisRef="Neh.9.15">Neh 9:15</reference>, are similar to Deu 1:10. The taking possession of Canaan is spoken of in Neh 9:24. ותּכנע recalls Deu 9:3. כּרצונם, according to their pleasure, comp. Dan 8:4. Fortified cities, as Jericho and Ai. <div eID="gen6609" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen6610" type="x-p"/> But even in that good land the fathers were disobedient: they rejected the commands of God, slew the prophets who admonished them, and were not brought back to the obedience of God even by the chastisement inflicted on them, till at length God delivered them into the hands of Gentile kings, though after His great mercy He did not utterly forsake them. - <reference osisRef="Neh.9.26">Neh 9:26</reference> “And they were disobedient, and rebelled against Thee, and cast Thy law behind their backs, and slew Thy prophets which testified against them to turn them to Thee, and they wrought great provocations. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.27">Neh 9:27</reference> And Thou deliveredst them into the hand of their oppressors, so that they oppressed them; and in the time of their oppression they cried unto Thee. Then Thou heardest them from heaven, and according to Thy manifold mercies Thou gavest them deliverers, who delivered them out of the hand of their oppressors. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.28">Neh 9:28</reference> And when they had rest, they again did evil before Thee. Then Thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, so that they had dominion over them; and they cried again unto Thee, and Thou heardest from heaven, and didst deliver them according to Thy great mercy, many times.”
entries.89e03ae8c7c9f68f53325176f3b4f248ec4aab6e: <reference osisRef="Neh.9.26">Neh 9:26</reference> <div eID="gen6610" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen6611" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="Neh.9.26">Neh 9:26</reference> again contains, like <reference osisRef="Neh.9.16">Neh 9:16</reference>, a general condemnation of the conduct of the children of Israel towards the Lord their God during the period between their entrance into Canaan and the captivity, which is then justified by the facts adduced in the verses following. In proof of their disobedience, it is mentioned that they cast the commands of God behind their back (comp. 1Ki 14:19; <reference osisRef="Ezek.23.35">Eze 23:35</reference>), and slew the prophets, e.g., Zechariah (<reference osisRef="2Chr.24.21">2Ch 24:21</reference>), the prophets of the days of Jezebel (1Ki 18:13; 1Ki 19:10), and others who rebuked their sins to turn them from them. בּ העיד, to testify against sinners, comp. 2Ki 17:13, 2Ki 17:15. The last clause of <reference osisRef="Neh.9.26">Neh 9:26</reference> is a kind of refrain, repeated from Neh 9:18.
entries.880ba56f5c65033639cafb1343fbca91d51a5430: <reference osisRef="Neh.9.27-Neh.9.28">Neh 9:27-28</reference> <div eID="gen6611" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen6612" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="Neh.9.27">Neh 9:27</reference> and <reference osisRef="Neh.9.28">Neh 9:28</reference> refer to the times of the judges; comp. Jdg 2:11-23. מושׁיעים are the judges whom God raised up to deliver Israel out of the power of their oppressors; comp. Jdg 3:9. with Neh 2:16. עתּים רבּות, multitudes of times, is a co-ordinate accusative: at many times, frequently; רבּות like Lev 25:51.
entries.b0c05bd488de4759cfe34df2800640eeb6acc5c8: <reference osisRef="Neh.9.29-Neh.9.30">Neh 9:29-30</reference> “And testifiedst against them, to bring them back again to Thy law; yet they hearkened not to Thy commandments, and sinned against Thy judgments, which if a man do he shall live in them, and gave a resisting shoulder, and hardened their neck, and would not hear. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.30">Neh 9:30</reference> And Thou didst bear with them many years, and didst testify against them by Thy Spirit through Thy prophets; but they would not hearken, therefore Thou gavest them into the hand of the people of the lands. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.31">Neh 9:31</reference> Nevertheless in Thy great mercy Thou didst not utterly consume them, nor forsake them; for Thou art gracious and merciful.” <div eID="gen6612" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen6613" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="Neh.9.29">Neh 9:29</reference> and <reference osisRef="Neh.9.30">Neh 9:30</reference> treat of the times of the kings. בּהם ותּעד is the testimony of the prophets against the idolatrous people; comp. Neh 9:26. וּבמשׁפּטיך is emphatically prefixed, and taken up again by בּם. The sentence, which if a man do he shall live in them, is formed upon <reference osisRef="Lev.18.5">Lev 18:5</reference>, comp. Eze 20:11. On the figurative expression, they gave a resisting shoulder, comp. Zec 7:11. The simile is taken from the ox, who rears against the yoke, and desires not to bear it; comp. Hos 4:16. The sentences following are repeated from Neh 9:16. עליהם תּמשׁך is an abbreviated expression for חסד משׁך, <reference osisRef="Ps.36.11">Psa 36:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.109.12">Psa 109:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.31.3">Jer 31:3</reference>, to draw out, to extend for a long time favour to any one: Thou hadst patience with them for many years, viz., the whole period of kingly rule from Solomon to the times of the Assyrians. The delivering into the power of the people of the lands, i.e., of the heathen (comp. Psa 106:40.), began with the invasion of the Assyrians (comp. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.32">Neh 9:32</reference>), who destroyed the kingdom of the ten tribes, and was inflicted upon Judah also by means of the Chaldeans.
entries.254c8b0e0b14f089fe4bbe39ab9ec8e1c0ea7aa6: <reference osisRef="Neh.9.31">Neh 9:31</reference> <div eID="gen6613" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen6614" type="x-p"/> But in the midst of these judgments also, God, according to His promise, <reference osisRef="Jer.4.27">Jer 4:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.5.10">Jer 5:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.18">Jer 5:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.30.11">Jer 30:11</reference>, and elsewhere, did not utterly forsake His people, nor make a full end of them; for He did not suffer them to become extinct in exile, but preserved a remnant, and delivered it from captivity.
entries.5f45129bc9bbfb7f44258bb4e880d1d86a8f478a: <reference osisRef="Neh.9.32">Neh 9:32</reference> <div eID="gen6614" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen6615" type="x-p"/> May then, God, who keepeth covenant and mercy, now also look upon the affliction of His people, though kings, rulers, priests, and people have fully deserved this punishment; for they are now bondmen, and in great affliction, in the land of their fathers. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.32">Neh 9:32</reference> “And now, our God, the great, the mighty, and the terrible God, who keepest covenant and mercy, let not all the trouble that hath come upon us, on our kings, our princes our priests, our prophets, and our fathers, and on all Thy people, since the times of the kings of Assyria unto this day, seem little to Thee. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.33">Neh 9:33</reference> Thou art just in all that is come upon us; for Thou hast done right, but we have done wickedly. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.34">Neh 9:34</reference> And our kings, our princes, our priests, and our fathers have not kept Thy law, nor hearkened to Thy commandments and Thy testimonies, wherewith Thou didst testify against them. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.35">Neh 9:35</reference> And they have not served Thee in their kingdom, and in Thy great goodness that Thou gavest them, and in the large and fat land which Thou gavest up to them, and have not turned from their wicked works. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.36">Neh 9:36</reference> Behold, we are now bondmen; and the land that Thou gavest unto our fathers to eat the fruit thereof, and the good thereof, behold, we are bondmen in it. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.37">Neh 9:37</reference> And it yieldeth much increase unto the kings whom Thou hast set over us because of our sins; and they have dominion over our bodies, and over our cattle at their pleasure, and we are in great distress.” The invocation of God, <reference osisRef="Neh.9.32">Neh 9:32</reference>, like that in <reference osisRef="Neh.1.5">Neh 1:5</reference>, is similar to Deu 10:17. לפניך ימעט אל stands independently, the following clause being emphasized by את, like e.g., <reference osisRef="Neh.9.19">Neh 9:19</reference> : Let not what concerns all our trouble be little before Thee; comp. the similar construction with מעט in Jos 22:17. What seems little is easily disregarded. The prayer is a <hi type="italic">litotes</hi>; and the sense is, Let our affliction be regarded by Thee as great and heavy. The nouns למלכינוּ, etc., are in apposition to the suffix of מצאתנוּ, the object being continued by ל.
entries.cda68b1e41938daf17868253213e1c1cfbe10cc7: <reference osisRef="Neh.9.33-Neh.9.34">Neh 9:33-34</reference> <div eID="gen6615" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen6616" type="x-p"/> Thou art just: comp. <reference osisRef="Neh.9.8">Neh 9:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Deut.32.4">Deu 32:4</reference>; Ezr 9:15. כּל על, upon all, i.e., concerning all that has befallen us; because their sins deserved punishment, and God is only fulfilling His word upon the sinners. In <reference osisRef="Neh.9.34">Neh 9:34</reference>, את again serves to emphasize the subject. In the enumeration of the different classes of the people, the prophets are here omitted, because, as God’s witnesses, they are not reckoned among these who had transgressed, though involved (<reference osisRef="Neh.9.32">Neh 9:32</reference>) in the sufferings that have fallen on the nation.
entries.a90654b122138321034d2a6887413f113314c8b6: <reference osisRef="Neh.9.35">Neh 9:35</reference> (<reference osisRef="Neh.10.1">10:1</reference>) הם are the fathers who were not brought to repentance by God’s goodness. בּמלכוּתם, in their independent kingdom. הרב טוּבך, Thy much good, i.e., the fulness of Thy goodness, or “in the midst of Thy great blessing” (Bertheau). The predicate הרחבה, the wide, extensive country, is derived from Exo 3:8. In Neh 9:36., the prayer that God would not lightly regard the trouble of His people, is supported by a statement of the need and affliction in which they still are. They are bondmen in the land which God gave to their fathers as a free people, bondmen of the Persian monarchs; and the increase of the land which God appointed for His people belongs to the kings who rule over them. The rulers of the land dispose of their bodies and their cattle, by carrying off both men and cattle for their use, e.g., for military service. כּרצונם like Neh 9:24.  <chapter eID="Neh.9"/> <div eID="gen6616" type="x-p"/>

                  <ns0:p n="22">22 Moreover, thou gavest them kingdoms, and na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions, and didst divide them into corners <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>into a corner.</ns0:hi> But the singular number is very commonly put for the plural. This is understood, either, 1. Of the Israelites, to whom God divided by lot <ns0:hi>the Kingdoms</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Nations</ns0:hi> last mentio<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned, and gave them all the <ns0:hi>corners,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>sides</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>quarters</ns0:hi> (for all these the word signifies) of their land. Or, rather 2. Of <ns0:hi>the</ns0:hi> heathen <ns0:hi>Nations,</ns0:hi> whom God in a great measure destroyed and the remain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ders of them <ns0:hi>he dispersed into corners;</ns0:hi> that whereas before the Israe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lites came, they had large habitations and dominions, now they were cooped up into corners, some of them into one Town or city, and some into another, in the several corners of their land, as indeed we find them afterward, whilest the Israelites dwelt in a large place, and had the possession of their whole land, some few and small parcels excepted. Compare <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 31. 26. where the like phrase is used in the same sense.</ns0:note>: so they possessed the land of Sihon <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Numb. 21. 21. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> and the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="23">23 Their children also multipliedst thou as the stars of heaven, and broughtest them into the land, concer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning which, thou hadst promised to their fathers that they should go in to possess it.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="24">24 So the children went in and possessed the land, and thou subduedst before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and gavest them into their hand, with their kings, and the people of the land, that they might do with them <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>accor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ding to their will.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> as they would.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="25">25 And they took strong cities, and a fat land, and possessed houses full of all goods, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>cisterns.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> wells digged, vine<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />yards, and olive-yards, and <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>trees of food.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> fruit-trees in abundance: so they did eat, and were filled, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 32. 15.</ns0:note> became fat, and delighted themselves in thy great goodness <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> In all these comforts and blessings which by thy great goodness they obtained and enjoyed. <ns0:hi>f i. e.</ns0:hi> Neglected and despised them, would not regard nor observe them, whereas they should have had them continually before their eyes, to direct and govern them. Compare <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 50. 17. <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 23. 35.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="26">26 Nevertheless, they were disobedient, and rebel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led against thee, & <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Kin. 14. 9.</ns0:note> cast thy law behind their backs <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Of which see on <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 18. 5. <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 20. 11. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 10. 5. <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 3. 12.</ns0:note>, and slew thy <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Kin. 19. 10.</ns0:note> prophets, which testified against them, to turn them to thee, and they wrought great provoca<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="27">27 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Judg. 2. 14. & 3. 8. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> Therefore thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, who vexed them, and in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven: and according to thy manifold mercies thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="28">28 But after they had rest, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>they returned to d<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap> evil.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> they did evil again be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore thee! therefore leftest thou them in the hand of their enemies, so that they had the dominion over them: yet when they returned and cried unto thee, thou hear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dest <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> from heaven, and many times didst thou de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />liver them, according to thy mercies.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="29">29 And testifiedst against them, that thou mightest bring them again unto thy law: yet they dealt proud<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly, and hearkned not unto thy commandments, but sin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned against thy judgments (which if a man do, he shall live in them <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Of which see on <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 18. 5. <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 20. 11. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 10. 5. <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 3. 1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note>) and <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>
                           <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap> gave a with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />drawing <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>oul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> withdrew the shoulder, and har<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dened their neck <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Would not submit to thy yoke, like stub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />born oxen.</ns0:note>, and would not hear.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="30">30 Yet many years didst thou <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>protract over them.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> forbear them <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Thou didst delay to bring upon them these judgments which thou hadst threatned and they had deser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ved, and didst wait for their repentance.</ns0:note>, and testifiedst <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Kin. 17. 13.</ns0:note> against them by thy spirit <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>in the hand of thy prophets.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> in thy pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">By thy prophets who spake to them by the inspiration of thy holy Spirit, whom therefore they should have obeyed.</ns0:note>: yet would they not give ear <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Would not obey, them nor would they vouchsafe so much as to hear them.</ns0:note>: therefore ga<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vest thou them into the hand of the people of the lands.<ns0:note place="margin">2 Chr. 36. 15.</ns0:note>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="31">31 Nevertheless for thy great mercies sake thou didst not utterly consume them, nor forsake them, for thou <ns0:hi>art</ns0:hi> a gracious and merciful God.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="32">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:374" />32. Now there ore our God, the great, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 3<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>. 6, 7.</ns0:note> the migh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty, and the terrible God, who keepest covenant and mercy <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Covenanted mercy or thy covenant of mercy and peace<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Or he adds <ns0:hi>mercy,</ns0:hi> because the <ns0:hi>covenant</ns0:hi> in its self was not a sufficient ground of hope, because they having so basely broken it, God was discharged from keeping it, and therefore they fly to Gods free and rich <ns0:hi>mercy</ns0:hi> for relief.</ns0:note>: let not all the <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>weari<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> trouble seem little before thee <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Do not thou account it small and insufficient for our punishment, and that it is fit to continue and encrease it.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>that hath found us.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> that hath come upon us, on our kings, on our princes, and on our priests<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and on our prophets, and on our fathers, and on all thy people since the time of the kings of Assyria <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Strictly and properly so called; for from them was the beginning of all the calamities both of <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> and of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> as appears, from 2. <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 15. 19. and 18. 13. Or, the kings of Ba<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bylon, so called, a <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 33. 11.</ns0:note>, unto this day.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="33">33 Howbeit, thou <ns0:hi>art</ns0:hi> just in all that is brought up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on us: for thou hast done right, but we have done wickedly.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="34">34 Neither have our kings, our princes, our priests, nor our fa<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>thers kept thy law, nor hearkened unto thy commandments, and thy testimonies, wherewith thou didst testifie against them.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="35">35 For they have not served thee in their kingdom, and in thy great goodness that thou gavest them, and in the large and fat land which thou gavest before them <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Which thou didst lay open to their view and posses<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion removing their enemies and all impediments out of the way.</ns0:note>, neither turned they from their wicked works.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="36">36 Behold, we <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> servants this day, and <ns0:hi>for</ns0:hi> the land that thou gavest unto our fathers, to eat the fruit thereof, and the good thereof, behold, we <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> servants in it <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">In that land wherein heretofore under thee and by thy favour we were rightful lords and owners.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="37">37 And it yieldeth much increase unto the kings whom thou hast set over us <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">We plow and sow and labour, and thou givest thy blessing to our indeavors; and yet in a great measure this is not for our selves, as formerly it was, but for our kings, to whom we pay great & hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vy tributes for these things: of which see <ns0:hi>Ezra</ns0:hi> 6. 8. and 7. 24.</ns0:note>, because of our sins: also they have dominion over our bodies, and over our cat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tel <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Pressing or foreing both us and our beasts to go and do what they please.</ns0:note>, at their pleasure, and we <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> in great distress.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="38">38 And because of all this <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Because all this misery lies upon us for our sins, we do heartily repent of them & resolve to forsake them.</ns0:note>, we make a sure <ns0:hi>cove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nant</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>we faithfully promise</ns0:hi> and engage our selves to future obedience.</ns0:note>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and write <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> and our princes, Levites, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> priests <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. are <ns0:hi>at the sealing,</ns0:hi> or, <ns0:hi>sealed.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> seal <ns0:hi>unto it.</ns0:hi>
